exposure: positive anti-CMV IgG and negative anti-CMV IgM in pregnant women
cohort: A total of 695 pregnant women with positive anti-CMV IgG and negative anti-CMV IgM during the first or second trimester who delivered by Cesarean section were enrolled, resulting in 823 newborns.
finding: Transplacental CMV transmission can occur in offspring of pregnant women with positive anti-CMV IgG and negative anti-CMV IgM, but the observed long-term sequelae (hearing, vision, and neurodevelopment) appear to be minimal.
birth_weight: N/A (intrauterine growth restriction mentioned for one case, but no specific weight range for the cohort)
gest_age: Both full-term (85.5%) and premature (14.5%) pregnancies were included; one neonate with CMV transmission was born at 30+2 weeks gestational age.
